- If sentiment is consistently low or negative (≤0.3) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward movement.
- When model shows strong upward trend (e.g., >90.0) with sentiment neutral or positive, actual prices often correct downward; apply downward bias correction if sentiment drops below 0.6.
- If model forecast is flat or slightly rising but true outcome shows sharp drop (e.g., >10% from prior day), consider lagged correction: reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- Overshoot after spikes (e.g., model jumps to 90+ after 85–90) often leads to sharp correction; cap forecast at 10% below peak if sentiment is weak or negative.
- Mean reversion observed when model overestimates (e.g., 90+ for 5+ days) and true outcome drops 5–15% — apply downward adjustment proportional to sentiment decay.
- If sentiment history shows recent volatility (e.g., 0.0–0.2) and model is flat, expect sharp reversal; forecast should be slightly below recent low or trend line.
- For 30-day horizon, if model is consistently above 90 and sentiment is weak, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until sentiment improves or price drops.
